_doc: What each case's main.c measures relative to the main.ts every TS runtime runs. same = same algorithm and allocations. suppressed = volatile / noinline / asm deliberately block the optimisation clang would otherwise do, so the c row is a floor for that operation, not for the hardware. different = c does less or other work (lazy split where JS materialises, a hand-written scanner where JS runs a regex engine). libc = the work is delegated to a libc routine with its own algorithm and cost model (regexec, setjmp). hardev/autorun/bench_latest.sh refuses a c row that is not listed here and only pools `same` rows into medianVsCSameProgram. lead = the measured mechanism by which tr does less work than a `same` comparator; a lead over 20% without one is reported as unexplained.

ackermann.lead: tr inlines the self-call one level, which clang does not: more instructions retired, fewer cycles

popcount.why: hand-rolled Kernighan loop, no hardware popcount intrinsic; tr folds the whole loop into a ctpop superinstruction

mandelbrot.why: FMA contraction disabled to match rust rounding

collatz.why: u64 n & 1 and n >>= 1 where main.ts needs f64 % 2 and / 2

generic-id-1m.why: noinline loop_sum keeps the sum out of the push loop

generic-pair-1m.why: the pair never escapes, so it is a local struct; clang is free to reduce the loop

split-only-100k.why: materialises the slice array every iteration; tr proves the array is only measured and answers a count

map-str-100k.why: SipHash-1-3 open addressing as std HashMap; tr hashes keys with FNV-1a

array-copy-1m.why: volatile / asm per element block the memcpy the loop is

array-map-1m.why: noinline callback + volatile keep the call indirect

array-sum-1m.why: volatile / asm per element block vectorisation

class-method-100k.why: volatile + asm keep both per-iteration heap objects alive

str-concat-ascii-100k.why: volatile + asm keep the per-iteration buffer, which clang would fold

i64-to-str-100k.why: volatile + asm keep each formatted buffer

json-stringify-100k.why: grows each record buffer from capacity 0 by realloc and escapes the key names at run time; not the fast way to write this in C

rpn-eval-100k.why: lazy in-place tokeniser and a fixed stack array; JS split materialises an array

csv-trim-100k.why: lazy in-place scan; JS split materialises an array

csv-rebuild-100k.why: lazy scan with one malloc per field; JS split materialises an array

throw-catch-100k.why: setjmp / longjmp stands in for throw / catch; macOS setjmp saves the signal mask

regex-dfa-anchored-100k.why: POSIX regcomp / regexec with snprintf input construction

regex-dfa-uflag-100k.why: hand-written utf-8 decode + \p{L} range table; no regex engine

regex-wireback-minlit-100k.why: POSIX regexec; no match array, index or input props

array-any-indexed-100k.why: fixed struct array with a length field where main.ts reads an any[] and dispatches on the tag; clang removes most of the loop (work-only 0.04 ms)

multibyte-concat-100k.why: uint16_t buffer holds the UTF-16 code units a JS string has; appended in place with doubling capacity

async-fn-call-100k.why: hand-written microtask queue + reaction list; enqueues and resumes as the spec orders
async-fn-call-100k.caveat: tr does not suspend at these awaits yet (P-LOOP 4): the drain runs inline in an order the spec forbids, so tr's lead here is not a ceiling reading

promise-all-1k.caveat: tr does not suspend at these awaits yet (P-LOOP 4): the drain runs inline in an order the spec forbids, so tr's lead here is not a ceiling reading

promise-await-100k.caveat: tr does not suspend at these awaits yet (P-LOOP 4): the drain runs inline in an order the spec forbids, so tr's lead here is not a ceiling reading

promise-chain-1k.caveat: tr does not suspend at these awaits yet (P-LOOP 4): the drain runs inline in an order the spec forbids, so tr's lead here is not a ceiling reading

promise-then-100k.caveat: tr does not suspend at these awaits yet (P-LOOP 4): the drain runs inline in an order the spec forbids, so tr's lead here is not a ceiling reading

split-materialize-1m.why: split counts the separators, then allocates one array of pointer-and-length views into the line, the shape of tr's split block of views, no copy per field; rebuilt is appended in place with doubling capacity

throw-unwind-depth8-1m.why: sigsetjmp / siglongjmp without the signal mask stands in for throw / catch; every frame with a finally has its own jump buffer and re-raises; the thrown object is heap-allocated

str-build-1mb.why: byte buffer appended in place with doubling capacity from 8, a fresh buffer every round

tokenizer-parser-eval-10k.why: one malloc per token and per AST node, token array grown by doubling, tree and tokens freed per line; the parser state never escapes, so it is a local struct

regex-capture-exec-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures are written as their own heap strings and the digits parsed with strtoll from the captured one, but only the length of the key is read, so clang removes that allocation

regex-replace-callback-1m.why: a hand-written matcher for ([a-z]+)=(\d+) stands in for a general regex engine; both captures and the replacer's result are their own heap strings, the output is appended in place with doubling capacity from 8
